title: Everyone Knows How to Catch a Pig

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: The pig has escaped and everyone shouts advice at the villager chasing it: follow every piece of advice, or ignore everyone.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The big pig has escaped, again, and (subject) is chasing it around the village. Every single person (subject.he/she) passes shouts advice. "Go left!" "No, right!" "Wave your arms!" "Don't wave your arms!" "Throw a mango!" "Sing to it!" (friend) is running alongside (subject.him/her), also shouting advice.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) goes left, then right, waves (subject.his/her) arms, stops waving (subject.his/her) arms, throws a mango and starts singing. The pig stops dead and stares at (subject.him/her). The whole village goes quiet. Then the pig eats the mango and walks calmly back into its pen. Nobody can agree whose advice worked. Everyone is sure it was theirs.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) stops running, sits down on a log and waits. The pig, confused that nobody is chasing it any more, wanders over to see what's going on. (subject) puts a rope round its neck. The whole village stares. "How did you know to do that?" asks (friend). "I didn't," says (subject). "I was tired."
